measures.title: Drug Possession Penalty Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to the possession of a weapon.

issues.rationale: Introduced text rewrites Subsection 76-10-503(3) so that a Category II restricted person who possesses a firearm is guilty of a class A misdemeanor rather than a third degree felony when the only basis for the restriction is unlawful possession of marijuana without intent to produce, manufacture, or dispense it. The operative change is a graded reduction of a criminal penalty, which is what justice_reform carries.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Stoddard moved to pass H.B. 27 out favorably.

measures.title: Tax Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies state tax provisions.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text cuts the individual income tax rate and the corporate franchise tax rate, and removes the state sales and use tax on food and food ingredients contingent on a constitutional amendment. Three separate rate or base reductions in one instrument, all in the same direction, make this the clearest tax-cut vote in the 2023 committee bucket.

The same enrolled text also expands the state earned income tax credit and raises the income phase-out thresholds on the social security benefits credit. These are distinct provisions from the rate cuts and they target lower and middle income filers specifically rather than all filers, so they earn a second, narrower key.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Christofferson moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 54 out favorably.

measures.title: Waiver of Punitive Damages Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses agreements to waive or limit liability for punitive damages.

issues.rationale: First substitute text provides that a court may not enforce a provision of an agreement that waives or limits a party's liability for punitive damages, with an exception for depository institutions. Removing the ability to contract out of punitive damages exposure is a direct increase in the accountability a company faces in court, and the single carve-out does not reverse the rule.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Abbott moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 64 out favorably.

measures.title: School Assembly Notice Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires prior parental notice of certain school assemblies.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text requires a local education agency to notify a parent before a school assembly that addresses certain topics and to describe the assembly's content, so that the parent can act on the notice. The provision hands parents advance information and a decision they did not previously have, which is the edu_parental fight stated plainly.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Johnson moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 82 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Hinkins moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 82 out favorably.

measures.title: Reverse Mortgage Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill makes changes to reverse mortgage requirements.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text shortens the reverse mortgage cooling-off period from seven days to five days during which the lender may not close the loan, and adds an exception letting a person initiate foreclosure without first sending the certified-mail notice and allowing 30 days to cure when the borrower is deceased. Every operative change reduces a duty the lender owes the borrower, so a yea vote weakens accountability rather than strengthening it.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Whyte moved to pass H.B. 94 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Ipson moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 94 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 94 out favorably.

measures.title: Prohibited Correctional Facility Items
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts provisions related to communication devices in correctional facilities.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text makes it a criminal offense to possess or transport a communication device at a correctional facility without authorization and sets the offense level. Creating a new crime with a new penalty is the direction tough_on_crime carries, and nothing in the bill reduces an existing penalty.

committeeActs.committee: House Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Walter moved to pass H.B. 129 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Prohibiting Sex Transitioning Procedures on Minors
measures.generalProvisions: This bill prohibits a health care provider from performing a medical procedure on a minor for the purpose of attempted sex transitioning or attempted sex change.

issues.rationale: First substitute text prohibits a health care provider from performing a sex characteristic surgical procedure on a minor and from providing hormonal transgender treatment to a minor who was not already receiving it, and makes a violation unprofessional conduct. The prohibition removes access to a category of care available only to transgender people, so a yea is a vote against lgbtq_rights.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Acton moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 132 out favorably.

measures.title: Sensitive Material Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends requirements and prohibitions regarding sensitive material within the public school system.

issues.rationale: Sixth substitute text requires an LEA to review instructional material a parent alleges is prohibited sensitive material, to remove material determined to be prohibited, to report determinations to the State Board of Education, and to terminate a contract with a vendor that provides prohibited sensitive material. The instrument puts the parent's complaint at the front of a mandatory removal process, which is the parental-control direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Johnson moved to pass 4th Substitute H.B. 138 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McKell moved to pass 6th Substitute H.B. 138 out favorably.

measures.title: High Cost Infrastructure Development Tax Credit Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the high cost infrastructure development tax credit.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text extends the high cost infrastructure development tax credit and broadens the eligible project definition to include the storage or production of all fuels and infrastructure for an underground mine. Widening a production tax credit from a narrow list of fuels to all fuels, plus mine infrastructure, is a direct subsidy for extraction and fuel production capacity.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lyman moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 144 out favorably.

measures.title: Crime Posting Restrictions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill identifies circumstances where it is a crime to fail to aid a crime victim.

issues.rationale: Introduced text makes it a criminal offense to fail to render reasonable assistance to a victim of a crime the person witnesses, and imposes penalties. It creates a new affirmative criminal duty backed by punishment where none existed, which is squarely the tough_on_crime direction.

A separate provision of the same introduced text prohibits a person from distributing a visual recording of a crime unless the person first reported the crime to law enforcement. That is a distinct provision from the duty-to-assist offense and it restricts publication of a recording rather than conduct at the scene, so it earns a second, narrow key against free_speech.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Clancy moved to pass H.B. 147 out favorably.

measures.title: Emergency Water Shortages Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses emergency shortages of water declared by the governor.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text enacts water use preferences during a declared temporary water shortage emergency, sets out how the state engineer applies those preferences, and provides for compensation of a water right holder whose use is curtailed. It gives the state an operative drought tool over how scarce water is allocated, which is the core of the water key.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Shipp moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 150 out favorably.

measures.title: Independent Election Evaluations
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires an independent attestation engagement in relation to certain election matters.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires the lieutenant governor to contract with an independent accounting firm to perform an attestation engagement evaluating the accuracy, validity, and completeness of election audits and results, and to make the report public. An outside attestation of the count, published, is the audit-and-verify direction that election_integrity carries.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Pierucci moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 155 out favorably.

measures.title: Electronic Information or Data Privacy Act Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions concerning electronic information or data privacy.

issues.rationale: First substitute text lets a law enforcement agency obtain a defined category of electronic information or data with an administrative subpoena rather than a warrant, and amends the notification a subscriber receives. Lowering the legal process required for the government to reach a person's electronic data reduces the protection the Electronic Information or Data Privacy Act gives, so a yea is a vote against privacy_rights.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hollins moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 158 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: School Fees Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends and enacts provisions related to elementary and secondary school fees.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text prescribes the fees an LEA may charge, prohibits an LEA from charging a general fee, and prohibits a fee for grade six remediation. The provisions take out-of-pocket charges off public school families for instruction the district must provide anyway, which strengthens the free public school guarantee rather than the private alternatives.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Grover moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 175 out favorably.

measures.title: Veterinary Practice Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill adds an exemption to the requirement for licensure under the Veterinary Practice Act.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text exempts a person who performs pregnancy testing on bovine animals from the licensure requirements of the Veterinary Practice Act. The exemption exists so ranch and dairy operations can have herd pregnancy testing done without hiring a licensed veterinarian, a direct reduction of an operating cost carried by agricultural producers.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Owens moved to pass H.B. 187 out favorably.

measures.title: Criminal Investigations of School Employees
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires certain administrative leave for school employees who are the subject of a criminal investigation.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires that a school employee placed on administrative leave during a criminal investigation receive a portion of salary during the leave, provides for back pay if the allegation is not substantiated, and requires repayment if it is. Guaranteed partial pay and back pay during an investigation is a job-security protection for the employee, which is a narrow but real gain on the worker side.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Clancy moved to pass H.B. 195 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Grover moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 195 out favorably.

measures.title: Voluntary Firearm Safekeeping Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the voluntary commitment of a firearm in cases of domestic violence.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text prohibits a law enforcement agency from returning a voluntarily surrendered firearm to a person who has become a restricted person or who has been arrested for a domestic violence offense, and requires the Department of Public Safety to produce a pamphlet on victim rights. Keeping a surrendered firearm out of the hands of a domestic violence arrestee is the gun_safety direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Ballard moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 199 out favorably.

measures.title: Teacher Parental and Postpartum Recovery Leave
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires local education agencies to provide paid parental and postpartum recovery leave to employees of a local education agency and establish a leave sharing mechanism.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text requires every local education agency to provide paid parental and postpartum recovery leave at least equivalent to what state employees receive, to establish a leave sharing mechanism, and to notify qualified employees. A mandate that an employer class provide paid leave it was not previously required to provide is the paid_leave fight with no ambiguity.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Dailey-Provost moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 229 out favorably.

measures.title: Center for Medical Cannabis Research
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates the Center for Medical Cannabis Research.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text creates the Center for Medical Cannabis Research within the University of Utah, gives it duties, requires the Department of Health and Human Services to work with the center on guidance for medical cannabis use, and allows the center to draw on the Qualified Patient Enterprise Fund. Standing up and funding a state medical cannabis research institution is an expansion of the medical cannabis program's footing.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Judkins moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 230 out favorably.

measures.title: Low Income Housing Property Tax Exemption
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends the definitions related to property tax exemptions in the Property Tax Act.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text sets the circumstances under which a private owner of property used as permanent supportive housing qualifies as a nonprofit entity for the exclusive use property tax exemption. The exemption lowers the carrying cost of permanent supportive housing specifically, which is a subsidy to housing for people who would otherwise be unhoused rather than a general tax change.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Owens moved to pass H.B. 231 out favorably.

measures.title: Mental Health Services for Adults
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to the provision of mental health services for adults.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires the Department of Health and Human Services to create a long-term statewide assertive community treatment team plan and modifies the grant program that funds the development of ACT teams. ACT teams are a delivered service for adults with serious mental illness, and the bill funds and plans their expansion rather than merely studying the question.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Plumb moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 248 out favorably.

measures.title: Social Worker Licensing Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions of the Social Worker Licensing Act.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text removes the examination requirement for licensure as a certified social worker or a social service worker and repeals the certified social worker intern position. Striking a licensure examination is a reduction of an entry barrier into a regulated profession, the same direction the shipped vocabulary uses gov_regulation for.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Kwan moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 250 out favorably.

measures.title: Property Tax Income Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions of the Property Tax Act.

issues.rationale: First substitute text raises the household income limit at which a claimant qualifies for the homeowner's credit and raises the limit for the renter's credit under the Property Tax Act. Raising both income ceilings puts the circuit-breaker relief in reach of more low-income owners and renters, which is the property tax relief direction.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 260 out favorably.

measures.title: Unemployment Insurance Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the Employment Security Act.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text identifies additional conduct that disqualifies an individual from receiving unemployment benefits, directs the Unemployment Insurance Division to make rules on ineligibility for failing to accept suitable work, and requires a website for employers to report suspected fraud. Each provision narrows eligibility or adds employer-side policing of claims, so a yea cuts against the worker side.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 283 out favorably.

measures.title: Governmental Entity Budget Transparency
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires certain government entities to disclose certain information relating to the government entities' budgets.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires certain state and local government entities to disclose specified information about their budgets. A new affirmative disclosure duty about how public money is budgeted is the gov_transparency direction with nothing in the instrument pulling the other way.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Maloy moved to pass H.B. 294 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Johnson moved to pass H.B. 294 out favorably.

measures.title: Utah Water Ways
measures.generalProvisions: This bill provides for the creation of a new nonprofit, statewide partnership addressing water.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text creates the Utah Water Ways statewide partnership, sets out its powers and duties, provides for the selection of its board and executive director, and addresses the role of water supply entities in it. Wave 4 already reviewed water as the key for a 2024 bill directing this same partnership's work, and this is the instrument that gives the partnership its water stewardship duties, so the same key and a narrow weight apply.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Snider moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 307 out favorably.

measures.title: Social Media Usage Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill regulates social media companies and the use and design of social media platforms.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text prohibits a social media company from using a design or feature that causes a minor to become addicted to its platform, authorizes a private right of action for damages and attorney fees, creates a rebuttable presumption of harm and causation in some circumstances, and prohibits waivers of the act. Private liability plus a presumption against the company is a direct increase in corporate accountability.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. McCay moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 311 out favorably.

measures.title: Suspect Metal Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns the theft of certain types of property.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text provides an increased penalty for the theft of certain suspect metals. Raising the offense level for an existing crime is the tough_on_crime direction, and no provision of the bill reduces a penalty.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Gwynn moved to pass H.B. 313 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Weiler moved to pass H.B. 313 out favorably.

measures.title: Event Permit Notification Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires a public entity to provide public notice for a permitted event with an adult theme.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text requires a public entity that issues a permit for an event with an adult theme to give public notice under defined conditions and sets out liability presumptions and limitations tied to that notice. Attaching a notice condition and a liability regime to a permit based on the expressive content of the event burdens the expression, so a yea is a vote against free_speech.

committeeActs.committee: House Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Walter moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 329 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Microenterprise Home Kitchen Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends the Microenterprise Home Kitchen Act.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires a political subdivision to allow a microenterprise home kitchen that meets the permit requirements to operate, limits the local regulations that may be imposed on it, and provides that the Microenterprise Home Kitchen Act supersedes a conflicting local regulation. It clears a local veto out of the way of the smallest class of food business, which is the econ_smallbiz direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Brammer moved to pass H.B. 331 out favorably.

measures.title: Local Policies for Course Content Transparency
measures.generalProvisions: This bill requires local education agency governing boards to establish student instruction transparency policies that include certain determinations.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires every LEA governing board to adopt a course content transparency policy, to publish the policy on the LEA website, and to give the State Board of Education an annual assurance with a link to it. Making course content visible to the parents of enrolled students, by mandatory published policy, is the parental-information side of the edu_parental fight.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Birkeland moved to pass H.B. 344 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Birkeland moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 344 out favorably.

measures.title: Voter Affiliation Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses voting in primary elections, and changing party affiliation, for an election held in an even-numbered year.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text defines a change of affiliation deadline and, for an even-numbered year in which a presidential election is held, sets it at the day after the declaration of candidacy deadline instead of the long-standing spring cutoff, keeping April 1 for other even years; it also prohibits voting in the primaries of more than one registered political party for the same election. Moving the affiliation cutoff into early January in presidential years removes roughly ten weeks in which a voter could join a party in time to vote in its primary.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Bramble moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 365 out favorably.

measures.title: Utility Infrastructure Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the destruction of or tampering with a critical infrastructure facility.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text makes it a criminal offense to destroy, damage, or tamper with a critical infrastructure facility and a separate offense to impersonate a critical infrastructure facility officer or employee, while removing the same conduct from the lesser crime of criminal mischief. The instrument moves the conduct out of a general offense and into dedicated crimes at their own penalty levels.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Moss moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 370 out favorably.

measures.title: Working Farm and Ranch Protection Fund
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions related to the management, regulation, conservation, and use of natural resources.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text renames the LeRay McAllister Critical Land Conservation Program, establishes the LeRay McAllister Working Farm and Ranch Fund, and directs how a county may use rollback taxes and rollback tax funds. Re-pointing a standing conservation fund and county rollback revenue at keeping working farms and ranches in production is a direct subsidy of agricultural land use.

committeeActs.committee: House Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Ballard moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 371 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Clinical Health Care Provider Grant Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates a grant program for healthcare providers that provide opportunities for clinical experience to healthcare students.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates a grant program that pays health care providers to establish new clinical experience opportunities for health care students, and adds a reporting requirement. Paying for clinical training slots addresses the provider pipeline that determines whether care is available at all, which is a narrow but real gain on the healthcare side.

committeeActs.committee: House Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Dailey-Provost moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 386 out favorably.

measures.title: Incentives Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to tax credits.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text requires each state agency that issues a tax credit certificate to publish a webpage listing the names of claimants and the amounts they are eligible to claim, and requires the State Tax Commission to publish a page linking to every agency's list. Naming who receives a tax credit and how much, in public, is a disclosure of public money that did not previously exist.

committeeActs.committee: House Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Brammer moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 407 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Fillmore moved to pass 3rd Substitute H.B. 407 out favorably.

measures.title: State Employment Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to state employment.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text lets certain career service employees elect to convert to career service exempt status, establishes schedule AY positions as career service exempt, and converts schedule B employees who have not completed probation to exempt status when the position becomes schedule AY. Each provision moves state employees out of career service protection and under at-will management control.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Bolinder moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 412 out favorably.

measures.title: Initiative Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to a statewide initiative.

issues.rationale: First substitute text, contingent on the passage of a constitutional amendment, raises the share of the vote required for a statewide initiative that would increase taxes to pass. Wave 4 reviewed the identical mechanism in the 2024 session under voting_access with yea_opposes, and the same reasoning holds: it raises the bar on the ballot for one class of measure only.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Gricius moved to pass H.B. 422 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Fillmore moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 422 out favorably.

measures.title: Business Services Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill prohibits a company from coordinating with another to intentionally destroy certain companies by eliminating the viable options for the companies to obtain a product or service.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text prohibits a company from coordinating with another company to intentionally destroy certain companies by eliminating the viable options for obtaining a product or service, allows a civil action for injunctive relief or damages, requires an award of attorney fees to the prevailing party, and bars a court from reducing damages below actual damages. It is a private enforcement regime against coordinated corporate conduct.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Burton moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 449 out favorably.

measures.title: State Entity Restrictions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill prohibits the use of certain statements or materials by a state entity to determine employment, admission, or other benefits.

issues.rationale: First substitute text prohibits a state entity from using a prohibited submission, defined to reach diversity statements and similar required declarations, in determining employment, admission, or other benefits, with limited exceptions. Wave 4 reviewed end_dei for the same fight in the following session, and this instrument is the state-entity version of it.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Thurston moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 451 as amendment out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Government Operations and Political Subdivisions Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Johnson moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 451 out favorably.

measures.title: School Materials Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions regarding student access to pornographic or indecent materials within the public education system.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires an LEA to run a review when a parent alleges instructional material is prohibited by state law, to vote publicly and explain any determination to reinstate or preserve student access to challenged material, and requires the State Board of Education to review LEA determinations and to establish an age-appropriateness rating system by rule. The parent's challenge drives a process the LEA cannot resolve quietly.

committeeActs.committee: House Education Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Walter moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 464 out favorably.

measures.title: Office of the Attorney General Employment Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to employees of the Office of the Attorney General.

issues.rationale: Second substitute text provides that employees of the Office of the Attorney General hired after a specified date may not be given career service status, lets existing employees elect to convert to career service exempt status, and replaces removal protections with a review process the attorney general may adopt by policy. It converts a career service workforce into an at-will one under the office head's control.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Gricius moved to pass 2nd Substitute H.B. 466 out favorably.

measures.title: Government Entity Compliance Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses public reporting relating to certain obligations of a government actor.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel to publicly post information about reports owed to legislative committees and policies a government actor is required to adopt, requires the state auditor to post the same kind of information, and lets the state auditor inquire into whether a government actor has complied. It puts a public record of compliance where none existed.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Stoddard moved to pass H.B. 506 out favorably.

measures.title: Firearm Possession Revisions
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends the definition of a restricted person.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text rewrites the Category II restricted person definition in Section 76-10-503 so that a single non-violent, non-domestic-violence felony conviction no longer restricts firearm possession for life: it restricts only where there is a domestic violence or violent felony, multiple episodes, or a further felony or class A misdemeanor within seven years of completing the sentence. The net effect is to restore firearm possession to a class of people who were restricted before.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Ballard moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 507 out favorably.

measures.title: Great Salt Lake Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses management of the Great Salt Lake and related activities.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text clarifies which minerals carry royalties to the Great Salt Lake Account, provides royalties for certain elements and minerals extracted from the lake, expands the Division of Forestry, Fire, and State Lands' management responsibilities and rulemaking for the lake, and establishes emergency management responsibilities and powers over it. Revenue directed to the lake plus operative emergency authority over its management is a water-side gain.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Owens moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 513 out favorably.

measures.title: Inmate Program Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns programs for inmates.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires the Department of Corrections to use an inmate's earliest estimated release date when scheduling programs, to start an inmate in at least two programs as soon as the case action plan exists, to allow participation in more than one program at a time, to create an incentive program for completing programs, and to confer periodically with the inmate about progress. Guaranteed access to rehabilitative programming before release is the justice_reform direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Burton moved to pass H.B. 517 out favorably.

measures.title: Social Media Usage Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill establishes the Utah Digital Expression Act.

issues.rationale: First substitute text prohibits a social media company from censoring user expression, from suspending, banning, demonetizing, deprioritizing, or attaching an accuracy assessment to a user's content in defined circumstances, requires a published acceptable use policy and an appeal process, and provides a private right of action. Whatever its constitutional fate, the operative rule is a prohibition on removing user speech, and a yea is a vote for that rule.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Kyle moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 524 out favorably.

measures.title: Eyewear Sales Tax Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions related to the sales and use tax on corrective eyeglasses and contact lenses.

issues.rationale: Introduced text amends the definition of prosthetic device to include corrective eyeglasses and contact lenses, which has the effect of exempting them from the sales and use tax. It is a single narrow base exclusion rather than a rate change, but it removes a tax the state currently collects.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Dunnigan moved to pass H.B. 525 out favorably.

measures.title: Food Shopping History Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill allows certain government agencies to obtain records related to a customer's shopping history from food establishments.

issues.rationale: First substitute text allows the Department of Health and Human Services and local health departments to obtain records related to a customer's shopping history from a food establishment. Giving a government agency access to an individual's purchase records is a reduction of the privacy those records currently have, so a yea is a vote against privacy_rights.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Matthews moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 529 out favorably.

measures.title: Telemedicine Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to reimbursement for telemedicine services.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires a health insurer to reimburse a network provider for a telemedicine service at 90% or more of the rate paid for the equivalent in-person service when that provider also delivers the service in person in the state. A payment-parity floor is what determines whether providers offer telemedicine at all, so the mandate expands access to covered care.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Lyman moved to pass H.B. 534 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Student Drug Possession Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses public education discipline policies related to the possession or use of tobacco, electronic cigarette, or nicotine products.

issues.rationale: Introduced text requires an LEA to amend its conduct and discipline policies to address possession or use of a tobacco product, an electronic cigarette product, or a nicotine product, and allows a school to issue a citation to a student who possesses one on school property. Both provisions tighten the consequences for youth nicotine possession.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Burton moved to pass H.B. 536 out favorably.

measures.title: Water Usage Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses the watering of lawn or turf during a restricted period.

issues.rationale: Third substitute text requires a municipality or water supplier in the Great Salt Lake basin to adopt an ordinance, resolution, rule, or regulation prohibiting the use of culinary or pressurized secondary water to irrigate non-exempt lawn or turf during a restricted period, with listed exemptions, and expressly preserves stricter local limits. A mandatory outdoor watering restriction during shortage is the water key's core direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Brooks moved to pass 1st Substitute H.B. 538 out favorably.

measures.title: Weapon Purchase Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates a waiting period for the delivery of an assault weapon.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates a waiting period between the purchase of an assault weapon from a dealer and its delivery to the purchaser, with defined exceptions. Wave 4 reviewed gun_safety at the same weight for the 2024 waiting-period bill, and this is the same mechanism applied to one class of weapon.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Pitcher moved to pass S.B. 50 out favorably.

measures.title: Background Check Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses time frames applicable to the expungement of criminal records.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates graduated deadlines by which a law enforcement agency must expunge criminal records that qualify for automatic expungement, sets deadlines for criminal justice agencies on petition-based expungement, and clarifies that certain deadlines apply to a court's expungement order. Enforceable deadlines are what make an expungement right real rather than nominal.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Stoddard moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 58 out favorably.

measures.title: Abortion Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions relating to physician reporting requirements in connection with providing an abortion.

issues.rationale: Introduced text removes the provision requiring a physician to verify that a report has been made to law enforcement before performing an abortion on a woman who is pregnant as a result of rape or incest. Striking a precondition that stands between a patient and a lawful abortion widens access, so a yea is a vote for pro_choice.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass S.B. 88 out favorably.

measures.title: Public Contract Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill addresses public entity contract requirements.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text enacts Public Contract Boycott Restrictions, defines a boycott of the State of Israel, prohibits a public entity from contracting with a company that engages in one, and prohibits penalizing a company that agrees not to engage in one for the duration of a public contract. The definition and the contract bar are express state action against boycotts of Israel.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 97 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Burton moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 97 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: School Gender Identity Policies
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts provisions ensuring a parent's access to information related to a parent's child, including gender identity.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text requires each school and local governing board to ensure a parent's right to access the education record of the parent's child, including information related to gender identity, and prohibits a school or LEA from withholding that access. The instrument resolves a contested question of who controls information about a student in the parent's favor.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Vickers moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 100 out favorably.

measures.title: Local Agricultural Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies the authority of a political subdivision to enact regulations regarding animal enterprises and working animals.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text defines animal enterprise and working animal and, subject to exceptions, prohibits a municipality or county from adopting or enforcing an ordinance or regulation that prohibits or effectively prohibits the operation of an animal enterprise or the use of a working animal. It removes local authority to shut down livestock and working-animal operations.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Sandall moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 113 out favorably.

measures.title: Social Care Information Privacy Requirements
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates requirements for a person who collects, processes, shares, or provides individually identifiable social care information.

issues.rationale: First substitute text requires consent before individually identifiable social care information may be accessed or shared, sets out what that consent must include, and imposes information privacy and security requirements on any person who collects, processes, shares, or provides the information. A consent requirement plus security duties over a new class of sensitive records is a direct privacy gain.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Health and Human Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 130 out favorably.

measures.title: Sex and Kidnap Offender Registry Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill address registration on the Sex and Kidnap Offender Registry.

issues.rationale: First substitute text removes a felony conviction for enticing a minor from the list of offenses that require lifetime registration on the Sex and Kidnap Offender Registry. Shortening a lifetime registration requirement to the ordinary term is a reduction of a post-sentence penalty, which is the justice_reform direction.

committeeActs.committee: House Judiciary Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Acton moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 134 out favorably.

measures.title: Legislative Offices Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions governing staff offices of the Utah Legislature.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text clarifies the legislative auditor general's authority over project entities, taxed interlocal entities, the Utah Data Research Center, and independent corporations, authorizes the office to conduct systemic performance audits of executive branch entities and local education agencies, authorizes subpoenas to financial institutions and service by electronic transmission, and requires a public body that holds a closed meeting to give the office information on request. Every one of those extends the reach of the audit function over public money.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Business and Labor Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Chair Bramble moved to pass 2nd Substitute S.B. 136 out favorably.

committeeActs.committee: House Government Operations Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Gricius moved to pass 3rd Substitute S.B. 136 out favorably.

measures.title: Sexual Crime Modifications
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates the offense of nonconsensual removal of a sexually protective device.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates the criminal offense of nonconsensual removal of a sexually protective device and imposes criminal penalties for it. A new offense with new penalties is the tough_on_crime direction; nothing in the instrument reduces an existing penalty.

committeeActs.committee: House Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Hayes moved to pass 1st Substitute S.B. 178 out favorably as amended.

measures.title: Local Land Use Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill modifies provisions regarding referenda.

issues.rationale: Enrolled text disallows referral of a referendum to voters for a municipal land use law that passed by a unanimous vote of the local legislative body. It closes the ballot to voters entirely for a defined class of local law, which is the same restriction of direct-ballot participation that the shipped vocabulary carries under voting_access with yea_opposes.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Owens moved to pass S.B. 199 out favorably.

measures.title: Government Records Access and Management Act Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill makes changes related to the Government Records Access and Management Act (act).

issues.rationale: Enrolled text establishes a process for a governmental entity to petition the State Records Committee for relief against a vexatious requester, authorizes the legislative and judicial branches and the governor to set up their own such processes, provides that an entity need not create a document stating that a requested record does not exist, limits judicial review of a GRAMA appeal to the issues raised below, and requires an outside person claiming business confidentiality to indemnify the entity. The requester-side additions are procedural; the operative new powers all run against access.

committeeActs.committee: House Public Utilities and Energy Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Rep. Romero moved to pass 4th Substitute S.B. 231 out favorably.

measures.title: Electric Energy Storage Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill creates a tax credit for commercial entities to install energy storage systems in the state.

issues.rationale: Introduced text creates an income tax credit for a commercial entity that installs a commercial energy storage system, directs the Public Service Commission to make rules on qualification, and has the Office of Energy Development issue the certificate. Subsidising storage capacity is what makes intermittent clean generation dispatchable, and the credit is written for storage specifically.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass S.B. 249 out favorably.

measures.title: Conservation Tax Incentive Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts corporate and individual tax credits for the purchase and installation of water efficient landscaping and fixtures in new homes.

issues.rationale: Introduced text enacts nonrefundable corporate and individual tax credits for a homebuilder's purchase and installation of water efficient landscaping and fixtures in new homes, with a certificate process through the Division of Water Resources and an annual cap. Wave 4 reviewed water at the same weight for a 2024 bill incentivising water efficient landscaping, and this is the new-construction version of that incentive.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Revenue and Taxation Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Escamilla moved to pass S.B. 252 out favorably.

measures.title: Drug-induced Homicide Amendments
measures.generalProvisions: This bill concerns the offense of drug-induced homicide.

issues.rationale: First substitute text creates the offense of drug-induced homicide and defines the terms that establish it. It creates a homicide-level offense out of conduct previously charged under lesser provisions, which is the clearest form of the tough_on_crime direction.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Judiciary, Law Enforcement, and Criminal Justice Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Acting Chair Kennedy moved to pass S.B. 254 out favorably.

measures.title: Dedicated Infrastructure District Act
measures.generalProvisions: This bill enacts the Dedicated Infrastructure District Act.

issues.rationale: Introduced text enacts the Dedicated Infrastructure District Act, sets requirements for creating a district to finance infrastructure and improvements, provides for its board of trustees and charter, and allows the district to issue bonds and levy taxes subject to limitations and to a contest procedure. Wave 4 reviewed dev_district_finance for the 2024 instrument creating a bonding-and-taxing development district, and this is the general-purpose version of it.

committeeActs.committee: Senate Economic Development and Workforce Services Standing Committee
committeeActs.motion: Sen. Owens moved to pass S.B. 295 out favorably.
